key_findings.label: Top Adoption Barrier (SA): Halal Certification Uncertainty

survey.text: In the past 3 months, have you purchased any chilled or refrigerated ready-meals, meal kits, or prepared foods from a supermarket or online grocery in Saudi Arabia or Egypt?
options: Yes, I have purchased chilled ready-meals or meal kits
No, I have not purchased these products
survey.insight: Half the sample (40 out of 80 respondents) already buys chilled or refrigerated ready-meals, confirming a proven purchase habit in the target category before any new product is introduced.

survey.text: How appealing do you find the idea of Premium Plant-Based Ready-Meals, restaurant-quality, plant-based meals that are chilled and ready to heat in 15 minutes, available in your local market?
survey.insight: Average appeal sits at 5.26 out of 10, and the distribution is skewed: 38 respondents scored the concept 6 or above, while 39 scored it 4 or below, meaning the concept polarises opinion more than it broadly excites.

survey.text: If Premium Plant-Based Ready-Meals were available in Saudi Arabia and Egypt at premium supermarkets and online grocery platforms, how likely would you be to buy them?
survey.insight: 57% say they probably would buy, and a further 3% say they definitely would buy, giving a combined positive intent of 60%, while only 19 respondents (roughly 24%) lean toward not buying.

survey.text: What is the maximum price you would be willing to pay per serving of a Premium Plant-Based Ready-Meal? (Select the highest price you would consider acceptable, answer in your local currency.)
options: I would not pay for this product at any price
survey.insight: 35% of respondents accept the premium price band (SAR 29-38 / EGP 151-200), making it the single most chosen tier, and stacking the super-premium band (10%) on top means 45% of buyers are willing to pay SAR 29 or more per serving.

survey.text: What factors would make you hesitate before buying Premium Plant-Based Ready-Meals in Saudi Arabia or Egypt? Select all that apply.
options: Uncertainty about halal certification or religious compliance
Lack of trust in plant-based ingredients or unfamiliar food technology
Cultural preference for home-cooked or traditionally prepared meals
Limited availability in local supermarkets or online delivery platforms
Shorter shelf life of chilled products compared to frozen alternatives
Strong existing local competition offering similar or cheaper options
Low awareness of the brand, I have never heard of it before
Price is too high relative to local income levels
Concerns about nutritional adequacy compared to meat-based meals
survey.insight: Distrust of plant-based ingredients or unfamiliar food technology is the top barrier, cited by 63 respondents, followed closely by uncertainty about halal certification (59) and low brand awareness (51), signalling that trust and compliance credentials must be established before price or availability concerns are addressed.

survey.text: Which of the following chilled ready-meal, plant-based food, or premium prepared-food brands do you currently use or buy in Saudi Arabia or Egypt? Select all that apply.
options: Kiri / Almarai chilled meal ranges (Saudi Arabia)
Puck / Arla chilled food products (Saudi Arabia/Egypt)
International brands via Carrefour / Lulu Hypermarket / Noon
Local restaurant meal-delivery services (e.g. HungerStation, Talabat, Otlob)
None of the above, I do not currently buy these types of products
survey.insight: International brands bought via Carrefour, Lulu, or Noon lead with 50 mentions, and local delivery apps (HungerStation, Talabat, Otlob) follow at 44, showing that the most-used purchase channels are already online or large-format retail, which aligns with the proposed distribution strategy.

survey.text: In your own words, what changes or adaptations would Premium Plant-Based Ready-Meals need to make, in terms of flavours, ingredients, halal standards, packaging, portion sizes, or anything else, to feel like the right fit for Saudi Arabia or Egypt?
survey.insight: Thirty open-text verbatims were collected asking respondents what flavour, ingredient, halal, packaging, or portion-size changes the product would need to feel right for Saudi Arabia or Egypt.

survey.text: Have you purchased or seriously considered purchasing a fitness-class subscription (e.g., gym membership, boutique studio pass, or multi-class package) in the past 12 months?
options: Yes, I have seriously considered but not purchased
No, I have not considered this
survey.insight: All 5 respondents have purchase intent, 4 already bought a fitness-class subscription in the past 12 months and 1 seriously considered it, signaling a fully purchase-engaged directional sample.

survey.text: Which of the following best describes how you currently manage your fitness-class needs? (Select all that apply)
options: Monthly gym membership at a large chain
Boutique studio drop-in classes (pay per class)
I do not currently pay for fitness classes
survey.insight: Respondents actively use multiple purchase channels: 4 of 5 use multi-class bundles or studio memberships AND 4 of 5 also pay for boutique drop-in classes, suggesting overlap and willingness to spend across formats.

survey.text: At what price per month would a Premium Fitness Subscription be SO EXPENSIVE you would not consider buying it? (Enter amount in USD)
survey.insight: Verbatim price-too-expensive thresholds were collected from all 5 respondents; review individual responses to identify the ceiling above which the product is disqualified from consideration.

survey.text: At what price per month would a Premium Fitness Subscription be priced so high that, although it's not out of the question, you'd have to think hard about buying? (Enter amount in USD)
survey.insight: Verbatim 'think hard' price points were collected from all 5 respondents; these responses mark the upper boundary of the acceptable range before purchase friction rises sharply.

survey.text: At what price per month would a Premium Fitness Subscription be a BARGAIN, a great buy for the money? (Enter amount in USD)
survey.insight: Verbatim bargain price points were collected from all 5 respondents; these responses anchor the lower end of perceived good value for the subscription.

survey.text: At what price per month would a Premium Fitness Subscription be priced so low you'd feel the quality couldn't be very good? (Enter amount in USD)
survey.insight: Verbatim too-cheap price points were collected from all 5 respondents; these responses define the floor below which quality skepticism undermines purchase intent.

survey.text: At $49 per month, would you purchase a Premium Fitness Subscription?
survey.insight: At $49/month, purchase intent is near-universal, 4 of 5 respondents say they definitely would buy and 1 probably would buy, indicating strong demand at this price point.

survey.text: At $79 per month, would you purchase a Premium Fitness Subscription?
survey.insight: At $79/month, intent remains high but shifts slightly, 3 of 5 say probably would buy and 2 say definitely would buy, with no negative responses in this directional sample.

survey.text: At $119 per month, would you purchase a Premium Fitness Subscription?
survey.insight: At $119/month, conviction softens noticeably, 3 of 5 respondents drop to 'might buy' while 2 say probably would buy, suggesting $119 sits at the edge of comfortable willingness to pay.

survey.text: At $169 per month, would you purchase a Premium Fitness Subscription?
survey.insight: At $169/month, hesitation dominates, 3 of 5 respondents still say 'might buy' but 2 say probably would NOT buy, marking this as a likely price resistance zone.

survey.text: At $229 per month, would you purchase a Premium Fitness Subscription?
survey.insight: At $229/month, intent collapses, all 5 respondents express negative intent (3 probably would NOT buy, 2 definitely would NOT buy), making this price a clear ceiling in this sample.

survey.text: What is the absolute most you would pay per month for a Premium Fitness Subscription? (Enter amount in USD)
survey.insight: Absolute maximum willingness-to-pay figures were collected from all 5 respondents; review individual verbatims to identify the hard price ceiling each respondent set.

survey.text: If your current fitness solution increased its price by 20%, how likely would you be to switch to a Premium Fitness Subscription?
survey.insight: Switching likelihood after a 20% price increase in their current solution averages 3.4 out of 5 across all 5 respondents, with 3 rating it a neutral 3 and 2 rating it a 4, suggesting moderate but not urgent openness to switching.

ranked.option: App crashed or froze during ordering
Food was incorrect or missing items
Difficulty tracking my order in real time

verbatims: SwiftEats saves me time during hectic work days, and my last order came on time with everything correct. But the app does crash sometimes during lunch rush, which is frustrating when I'm ordering between meetings.

Most of the time it works fast and the food comes when promised. But the app sometimes freezes when I'm ordering during lunch, and I've had a couple of missing items that annoyed me. It's reliable enough for my routine but not perfect.

The app is convenient for my work lunch, but the last three orders were delayed 10 to 15 minutes past the promised time. That's frustrating when I only have a 30-minute break. I also had a missing item recently which required a refund request, and I'm not sure the app feels as reliable as I need it to be.

The app saves me time on nights when work runs late and my family needs to eat quickly. The delivery tracking is honest, so I know when food will arrive. That's worth a lot when I'm stressed and juggling work with family time.

The delivery speed is solid and prices are fair, which is what I need as a busy working father. But the app can be confusing sometimes and I got an incomplete order once, which shook my confidence a bit.
Fix the app crashes during peak hours. I also wish there were better filters for dietary preferences and healthy options, since I'm trying to make better meal choices for my family.

Fix the app crashes during lunch hours. I work long shifts and often place orders at peak times, so when the app freezes it wastes my time. Also, be clearer about which promotions actually apply to my orders because I get confused sometimes.

Fix the delivery timing. I order at 12:30 because I have exactly 30 minutes, and when food arrives 10 to 15 minutes late, my break is almost over. Also, double-check orders before they leave the restaurant so items don't go missing. The app tracking is okay, but the promises need to be kept.

Stop letting restaurants go offline while I'm in the middle of ordering. It's annoying when the app doesn't warn me earlier that a place is about to close for orders. And sometimes I'd like to see faster delivery options without paying surge prices.

Fix the app so it's easier to navigate without getting lost, and make sure orders are checked before they leave the restaurant. Late deliveries frustrate me when I'm hungry after a long day, so keep the speed up.

The app interface is straightforward and I can quickly find the restaurants I like (Arabic and Asian fusion). What makes it harder is when the app lags or freezes during busy lunch times, and I can't easily filter for healthier meals.

Normally it's straightforward because I order from the same restaurants every time, so I just find them and tap through. But when the app gets slow during lunch rush, it takes longer and feels clunky. The tracking could also be better so I know exactly when the driver is coming.

The app interface is straightforward and my favorites are saved, so I can place an order in about 30 seconds. No problem there. But once I order, tracking and knowing whether my food will arrive on time is where it gets confusing. The estimated delivery time keeps changing, and there's no real-time visibility.

The interface is straightforward. I can tap in my favorites, choose a restaurant, and pay in seconds. What slows me down is when restaurants are listed as open but then I find out they're actually closed once I'm mid-order.
The app loads fine and the menu is clear, but finding what I want and checking out takes more clicks than it should. The tracking part is okay but could show more detail about where my delivery is.

survey.insight: All 5 respondents described what made their order easy or hard; see verbatims for qualitative detail.

key_findings.label: Openness to Cat Hotel (Q3 Agree Rate)

survey.text: Do you currently own one or more cats?
options: No, I do not own a cat
survey.insight: 100% of the 10 respondents own at least one cat, and 60% own multiple cats. Multi-cat owners represent a higher-revenue opportunity per booking and may have more acute need for boarding solutions. However, with only 10 respondents, this distribution is likely a screener artifact rather than a market-level insight.

survey.text: Have you ever heard of or used a cat boarding or cat hotel service in Sharjah or nearby areas?
options: Yes, I have used one before
Yes, I have heard of it but never used it
No, I have never heard of such a service
survey.insight: Of the 4 respondents who answered Q2, 3 had heard of cat boarding but never used it, and 1 had never heard of it at all. This suggests the concept is known but barriers to trial exist, likely trust, availability, or perceived quality. This is a significant market-entry insight: the product must address why aware non-users haven't converted.

survey.text: How do you feel about leaving your cat at a dedicated Sharjah Cat Hotel while you travel or are away from home?
survey.insight: A unanimous 'Agree' response with no neutral or negative votes is encouraging, but the absence of 'Strongly Agree' responses and the tiny sample (n=4) limits confidence. The lack of variance also raises a social desirability bias concern, respondents may be answering what feels positive rather than what reflects true intent. A larger, anonymized sample is needed.

survey.text: How likely are you to book a stay at the Sharjah Cat Hotel for your cat in the next 6 months?
survey.insight: Three of four respondents gave a rating of 4 out of 5, and one gave a 3. No respondents rated below 3 or at 5, clustering intent in the 'likely but not certain' zone. A 3.75 average on a 5-point scale is a reasonable early signal but falls short of the 4.0+ threshold typically associated with strong purchase intent. This warrants pricing and barrier exploration.

survey.text: What features or services would be most important to you when choosing the Sharjah Cat Hotel for your cat?
survey.insight: Both '24/7 live camera monitoring' and 'Flexible pickup and drop-off times' were selected by all 4 respondents, making them table-stakes features. Veterinary support ranked second (3 of 4), and personalized play sessions came third (2 of 4). Grooming was selected by no one, suggesting it is not a primary driver in this segment. The MVP should prioritize cameras and scheduling flexibility before adding grooming as an upsell.

survey.text: Do you currently have or are you considering getting a pet in the next 6 months?
options: Yes, I currently have pets and am open to more
Yes, I am actively looking to get a pet
No, I am not interested in having pets
survey.insight: 50% are 'maybe considering,' 30% are actively looking, and only 10% said no outright. This is a warm audience for adoption marketing, but the dominant 'maybe' cluster means messaging needs to push undecided people over the line by addressing practical hesitations, not just emotional appeal. The single 'no' respondent and 10% current-owner-open-to-more suggest a real adoption funnel exists even in this tiny sample.

survey.text: How appealing do you find the idea of Cat Adoption based on the image presented?
survey.insight: The modal response is 3 (neutral), chosen by 5 of 10 respondents. Only 1 respondent gave a 5, and 1 gave a 1, showing limited polarization but also limited excitement. This suggests the image alone is insufficient as the primary ad creative, it needs supporting copy that addresses trust, health, and practicality to lift appeal. A creative refresh or A/B test with a warmer, more lifestyle-integrated image is warranted.

survey.text: Which of the following factors would most influence your decision regarding Cat Adoption?
survey.insight: Both 'Health and vaccination records' and 'Temperament and behavior' were selected by all 10 respondents, making them the universal purchase criteria. 'Adoption process and support provided' came in third at 70%, reinforcing that post-adoption reassurance matters. Critically, 'The cat's appearance and breed' was cited by only 1 respondent, meaning leading with visual appeal in ad creative is likely a strategic mismatch with what actually drives decisions.

survey.text: Cat Adoption would fit well with my lifestyle and living situation in the UAE.
survey.insight: Five respondents agreed and two strongly agreed that cat adoption fits their UAE lifestyle, which is encouraging. However, 2 respondents disagreed or strongly disagreed, and these objections, visible in Q5 verbatims, stem from cultural norms, multi-pet households, and rental restrictions. The 10% neutral adds further ambiguity. Ads should proactively address the 'is this right for my life here?' hesitation rather than assuming lifestyle fit is self-evident.

survey.text: What concerns, if any, would you have about Cat Adoption in the UAE?
survey.insight: Across 10 verbatims, vet affordability and animal health were mentioned in at least 5 responses; the UAE/GCC heat and indoor climate management appeared in 5+ responses; time constraints from demanding work schedules appeared in 4 responses. Two responses surfaced cultural or religious hesitations, one explicitly citing Islamic scholarly guidance, another citing tradition and dignity. One respondent also flagged landlord restrictions in Sharjah. Notably, two respondents appear to be located outside the UAE (Manama/Bahrain, Muscat/Oman, Jeddah/Saudi Arabia), which further compromises the geographic targeting of this study.

survey.text: How often do you travel for leisure or tourism in a given year?
survey.insight: All 10 respondents travel 3 or more times per year, meaning this sample over-indexes on the most enthusiastic potential users. While this is useful for early concept validation and feature prioritization, it does not represent casual or infrequent tourists who may represent a larger share of the addressable market. Results should be interpreted as 'best-case' enthusiasm, not market-wide demand.

survey.text: Have you ever faced difficulty finding a safe place to store your luggage while exploring a city during your travels?
options: No, but I can see it being an issue
No, it has never been a problem
survey.insight: 30% experience the problem frequently and 70% occasionally, meaning zero respondents said it has never been an issue. This is the strongest possible validation that the core problem exists and is felt by the target audience. No further problem validation is needed; the team can now focus entirely on solution validation and differentiation.

survey.text: How appealing do you find the concept of a Luggage Storage App that helps you locate nearby storage spots and compare pricing in real time?
survey.insight: Six out of ten respondents gave a perfect score of 5, and four gave a 4, there were no ratings below 4. This top-box concentration is a strong early indicator that the value proposition resonates clearly with frequent travelers. Caution: this enthusiasm likely reflects the homogeneous, highly-traveled sample and should be stress-tested with a broader, more diverse cohort before drawing definitive conclusions.

survey.text: Which of the following features would be most important to you when using a Luggage Storage App? (Select all that apply)
options: Real-time availability of nearby storage locations
User reviews and ratings of storage facilities
survey.insight: Real-time availability, secure and insured storage, and easy in-app booking and payment were selected by every single respondent, establishing them as table-stakes features that must be present at launch. Transparent pricing (90%) and user reviews (80%) are nearly as critical and should be included in the MVP rather than deferred to a later release. Any launch version missing the top three features will face immediate rejection.

survey.text: What, if anything, would prevent you from using a Luggage Storage App during your travels? Please share any concerns or suggestions.
survey.insight: Across all 10 verbatims, concerns cluster into three themes: (1) trustworthiness and insurance, multiple respondents explicitly said security is 'non-negotiable' and they need verified insurance coverage with clear liability limits; (2) pricing competitiveness, several respondents want to benchmark against hotel day-passes and other alternatives before committing; (3) UX friction, at least two respondents flagged that the app must require no more than 2-3 taps to book or they will abandon it. Secondary signals include social proof needs (peer reviews, trusted networks), niche use-case requirements (climate-controlled storage, calendar integration, branded/aesthetic venues for content creators), and data privacy concerns. These barriers are solvable but must be treated as launch-critical, not post-launch improvements.

survey.text: Do you currently purchase or use any men's grooming products (such as skincare, haircare, shaving, or beard care products) in the UAE?
options: Yes, I regularly buy men's grooming products
No, I do not purchase men's grooming products
survey.insight: Most respondents are active grooming buyers: 41 said they regularly purchase men's grooming products and 19 buy occasionally, meaning all 60 who qualified use these products at least sometimes.

survey.text: When buying men's grooming products, I always look for the best price or deals available.
survey.insight: Price sensitivity is moderate among this group. The average rating is 3.03 out of 5, and the single largest group (23 of 60) rated price-seeking at just 2, showing more respondents lean away from deal-hunting than toward it.

survey.text: I love trying new grooming products and brands before most other people do.
survey.insight: Early adoption of new grooming products is weak, averaging only 2.68 out of 5. The majority (21 of 60) gave this statement a 1, making it the most common single response.

survey.text: Once I find a grooming brand I like, I stick with it and rarely switch.
survey.insight: Brand loyalty is strong: the average is 3.77 out of 5, and 45 of 60 respondents rated this statement 4 or 5, meaning most men stick with brands they know rather than switching.

survey.text: Having my grooming products delivered automatically matters more to me than getting the lowest possible price.
survey.insight: Convenience carries moderate weight over price, with an average of 3.32 out of 5. The largest group (28 of 60) rated this a 4, suggesting delivery convenience is a meaningful but not dominant purchase factor.

survey.text: The grooming brands I use reflect my personal image and say something about who I am.
survey.insight: Grooming products carry personal identity value for many respondents, scoring an average of 3.45 out of 5. The top rating of 5 was the single most common individual response (18 of 60), though opinion is spread across the scale.

survey.text: I prefer grooming brands that are ethically produced and environmentally sustainable.
survey.insight: Sustainability is a weak purchase driver, averaging just 2.48 out of 5. A large 36 of 60 respondents rated it 2, and no one rated it 1, suggesting mild indifference rather than active rejection.

survey.text: How often do you purchase men's grooming products?
survey.insight: Purchase frequency is split between regular and infrequent buyers. The two largest groups buy about once a month (23 respondents) or every 4-6 months (22 respondents), while only 11 buy more than once a month.

survey.text: How much do you typically spend on men's grooming products per month (in AED)?
survey.insight: Monthly spend is spread across a wide range. The largest group (16 of 60) spends AED 150-299 per month, but 11 respondents spend AED 500 or more, showing a meaningful high-spend segment exists alongside 13 who spend less than AED 50.

survey.text: Which of the following men's grooming brands or retailers have you used in the past 6 months? (Select all that apply)
survey.insight: Nivea Men is the most widely used brand, chosen by 47 of 60 respondents, followed by Gillette (38) and Noon or Amazon multi-brand platforms (37). The Man Company (22) and Bulldog Skincare and Dove Men+Care (21 each) round out the mid-tier.

survey.text: Which of the following platforms or channels do you spend the most time on for entertainment or information? (Select all that apply)
survey.insight: YouTube dominates media consumption, selected by 55 of 60 respondents. Instagram (35) and LinkedIn (24) are the next most common platforms, while TikTok (18) and Facebook (19) have a meaningful but smaller reach.

survey.text: When choosing a men's grooming product or subscription, which of the following are most important to you? (Select up to 3)
options: Affordable price or value for money
Convenience of home delivery or auto-replenishment
Ability to discover new or exclusive products
Personalised recommendations for my skin or hair type
survey.insight: Product quality and effectiveness is the clear top purchase priority, selected by 56 of 60 respondents. Convenience of home delivery or auto-replenishment (29) and trusted brand name (28) are the next most cited factors, while natural or sustainable ingredients ranks last at just 7 selections.

survey.text: Does your organisation currently commission, purchase, or actively use market research services (e.g., consumer surveys, focus groups, data analytics, audience profiling)?
options: Yes, we regularly commission or use market research
Yes, occasionally or on a project basis
No, we do not use market research services
survey.insight: All 300 respondents confirmed their organisation regularly commissions or uses market research, making this a fully qualified sample of active buyers.

survey.text: When selecting a market research provider, I always compare prices and look for the most cost-effective option available.
survey.insight: Price comparison is not a strong habit among these buyers: the average score is 3.22 out of 7, and 233 of 300 respondents landed at the midpoint (3), suggesting most are neither systematic price-shoppers nor indifferent to cost.

survey.text: I am eager to adopt new market research methodologies and innovative data collection approaches before others in my industry do.
survey.insight: Appetite for new methodologies is moderate, with an average of 4.52 out of 10 and 212 of 300 respondents scoring exactly 4, indicating the majority sit just below the midpoint and are cautious rather than eager early adopters.

survey.text: Once I find a market research provider I trust, I prefer to continue working with them rather than switching to new ones.
survey.insight: Provider loyalty is similarly lukewarm, averaging 4.39 out of 10, with 175 of 300 respondents scoring 4, meaning most organisations do not strongly prefer sticking with a familiar supplier over exploring alternatives.

survey.text: For market research projects, getting fast turnaround and easy project management matters more to me than achieving the lowest price.
survey.insight: Speed and ease of project management clearly outweigh price as a priority: the average is 5.63 out of 10, and 201 of 300 respondents scored 5, with a further 62 scoring 8, showing consistent preference for efficiency over cost minimisation.

survey.text: The market research firms and data partners I work with reflect the professional reputation and credibility of my organisation.
survey.insight: Respondents moderately agree that their research partners reflect on their own organisation's credibility, scoring an average of 4.68 out of 10, with 215 of 300 at score 4 and 58 at score 7, pointing to a quiet but real reputational consideration in vendor selection.

survey.text: How frequently does your organisation commission or conduct market research projects?
survey.insight: Quarterly commissioning dominates research cadence: 164 of the 300 respondents commission research every few months, while only 11 do so more than once a month, and 23 do so monthly, confirming that most buying decisions are periodic rather than continuous.

survey.text: Which of the following market research providers or platforms has your organisation used in the past 12 months? (Select all that apply)
survey.insight: Kantar (278 organisations) and local or regional boutique firms (276) are the most widely used providers in the past 12 months, well ahead of YouGov (204), Ipsos (184), and Nielsen (173), showing that buyers combine global brands with local specialists rather than consolidating around a single provider.

survey.text: Which of the following best describes your current relationship with digital banking or neobank services?
options: I currently use a digital bank or neobank
I am considering switching to a digital bank or neobank
I use traditional banking but am open to digital alternatives
I have no interest in digital banking

survey.text: In your own words, which digital banking or neobank brands have you seen or heard advertised recently in the UAE?
survey.insight: Open verbatims show NovaBank mentioned explicitly by two respondents alongside Liv. by Emirates NBD and Wio Bank, and a third respondent placed it in a scroll-discovery context on Instagram. Two respondents could not name any specific brand, citing low attention to banking ads generally. The unaided recall rate of 60% is the clearest evidence that the campaign is cutting through in this segment.

survey.text: Which of the following digital banking or neobank brands do you recall seeing an advertisement for recently? Select all that apply.
survey.insight: Three of 5 respondents selected NovaBank in the aided recall question, making it the single most recalled advertiser in this set. One respondent selected "None of the above," and no one recalled Zand Bank. The result confirms the campaign is generating impression-level awareness, but the 40% who did not recall a NovaBank ad represent a meaningful gap given this is a pre-qualified, digitally active audience.

survey.text: Which digital banking or neobank brands are you aware of, even if you have never used them? Please type any that come to mind.
survey.insight: Verbatims show NovaBank mentioned by 4 respondents in the unprompted brand awareness question, with Liv. by Emirates NBD also appearing four times and Wio Bank and Mashreq Neo appearing three and two times respectively. Notably, one respondent associated NovaBank with "younger professionals," suggesting the brand's positioning is landing but may feel narrow to this mid-career segment. Brand differentiation is weak: multiple respondents said they could not articulate what sets each brand apart.

survey.text: Which of the following digital banking or neobank brands have you heard of? Select all that apply.
survey.insight: All 5 respondents recognized Liv. by Emirates NBD, reflecting the halo effect of its parent brand. NovaBank at 4 of 5 (80%) and Wio Bank and Mashreq Neo at 3 of 5 (60%) each are closely grouped. Zand Bank was recognized by only 1 respondent (20%). The gap between NovaBank's aided awareness (80%) and Zand Bank's (20%) illustrates the early lead the campaign has built in this segment.

survey.text: On a scale of 1 to 5, how familiar are you with NovaBank and its services?
survey.insight: Among the 4 respondents who provided a rating, 2 selected "Heard the name only" (2) and 2 selected "Know a little about it" (3). No one rated familiarity above 3. This signals the campaign has succeeded at name-planting but has not yet communicated enough substantive information about NovaBank's features or value proposition for this audience to form a deeper impression.

survey.text: On a scale of 1 to 5, how favourable is your overall impression of NovaBank?
survey.insight: Two respondents rated NovaBank as "Favorable" (4) and two as "Neutral" (3). The absence of any negative ratings is a meaningful floor-level signal: the brand has not generated skepticism or distrust in this audience. However, a mean of 3.5 with no respondents reaching "Very favorable" shows the campaign has not yet created genuine enthusiasm, only benign openness.

survey.text: Which of the following messages, if any, do you associate with NovaBank? Select all that apply.
options: A fully digital, app-first banking experience
Fast and easy account opening with no paperwork
Competitive rates and low fees for UAE residents
Built for the modern UAE lifestyle
survey.insight: Three of 5 respondents selected "Fast and easy account opening with no paperwork" as a NovaBank association, the highest-scoring message. "App-first experience," "competitive rates," and "built for the modern UAE lifestyle" each received 2 of 5 mentions. Critically, 2 respondents selected "None of the above," indicating the campaign is not landing a consistent narrative with a meaningful portion of its exposed audience. The message mix appears scattered rather than anchored to a single, memorable idea.

survey.text: On a scale of 1 to 5, how likely are you to consider NovaBank the next time you evaluate banking options?
survey.insight: Two of 4 raters chose "Likely" (4), one chose "Neutral" (3), and one chose "Unlikely" (2). The distribution is modestly positive but the wide confidence interval (2.31 to 4.19) reflects meaningful variance within this tiny sample. The result suggests the campaign is planting a consideration seed, but not a strong enough one to reliably pull NovaBank onto a short list without further touchpoints.

survey.text: On a scale of 1 to 5, how likely are you to open an account or sign up with NovaBank in the next three months?
survey.insight: One respondent rated intent at "Very unlikely" (1), one at "Unlikely" (2), and two at "Neutral" (3). No respondent rated intent at 4 or 5. This is the sharpest drop in the funnel: awareness and impression are passable, but no one in this sample is ready to open an account in the next three months. Incumbent bank inertia and the absence of a compelling near-term switching trigger are the most likely barriers.

survey.text: On which of the following platforms do you recall seeing or hearing about NovaBank? Select all that apply.
survey.insight: Three of 5 respondents recalled NovaBank on Instagram; two selected "None of the above." YouTube and TikTok received zero mentions. This aligns with the verbatim data in q2, where respondents described encountering NovaBank while scrolling Instagram for property and market content. The campaign appears to be well-placed for the channel but has not diversified its recall surface beyond a single platform.

survey.text: On a scale of 0 to 10, how likely are you to recommend NovaBank to a friend or colleague living in the UAE?
survey.insight: Only 2 of 5 respondents provided a numeric NPS rating (scores of 3 and 5), giving a mean of 5.25 with a confidence interval of 3.58 to 6.92. The low response rate within the question (rating_n of 4 vs. n of 5, with the distribution only reflecting 2 values in the breakdown) means this metric should be treated as directional only. A score clustering around the passive range (5) is consistent with the "neutral to cautiously favorable" pattern seen across q7 and q9.

key_findings.label: Device Sync as Top Decision Driver

survey.text: How familiar are you with products in this category?
Rate your overall interest in this concept.
survey.insight: All 5 respondents rated the concept exactly 4 out of 5, producing a mean of 4.0 with zero standard deviation and a tight confidence interval (4.0 to 4.0). The absence of any 5-ratings tells you the concept has not yet crossed from 'sounds useful' into 'I need this now.' The product team should treat 4.0 as a baseline to move, not a validation to celebrate.

survey.text: What would most influence your decision here?
survey.insight: Smartwatch sync (Apple Watch specifically) was mentioned by at least 3 of 5 respondents as a precondition for adoption, not a nice-to-have. Logging speed and schedule flexibility were each raised by 2 respondents, with one explicitly saying 'friction kills motivation fast.' Social or accountability features appeared in 2 verbatims, but both came with caveats about avoiding nagging notifications or gimmicky sharing, meaning the feature must be designed with restraint.

survey.text: How often do you use a ride-hailing app (such as Uber, Careem, or similar) in the UAE?
options: I have never used a ride-hailing app in the UAE

survey.text: When you think about ride-hailing brands available in the UAE, which ones come to mind? Please list up to 5 brands.
survey.insight: All 5 respondents named Uber and Careem unprompted. Bolt and inDriver appeared in 3 of 5 responses each, and Yango appeared once. the brand did not appear in any open-text recall response, meaning we have no spontaneous brand presence in this segment. Spontaneous recall is a leading indicator of habitual use and is extremely difficult to build without either a strong price signal or a memorable service moment.

survey.text: Which of the following ride-hailing brands in the UAE have you heard of? Select all that apply.
survey.insight: Even with the brand name shown on screen, 2 of 5 respondents did not recognize it. Careem and Uber both scored 100% aided awareness (5 of 5). inDriver reached 80% (4 of 5), and Bolt, Yango, and the brand each reached 60% (3 of 5). Being on par with Bolt and Yango in aided awareness is a warning sign given the relative marketing investment those brands represent.

survey.text: Of the ride-hailing brands in the UAE you have heard of, which would you consider using next time you need a ride? Select all that apply.
survey.insight: Every respondent who knew the brand still chose not to consider us for their next ride. Careem and Uber each captured 100% consideration (5 of 5). No other brand, including inDriver, Bolt, or Yango, received any consideration votes either. The implication is that the entire consideration set has collapsed to two players in this professional male Dubai segment, and the brand has not found a wedge.

survey.text: Of the ride-hailing brands in the UAE you would consider, if you had to choose just ONE for your next ride, which would you pick?
survey.insight: All 5 respondents selected Uber as their single top choice. Careem, which matched Uber on consideration, did not win a single first-choice vote. This reveals that Careem is a backup brand rather than a primary one, and the brand is not even in that backup category. For our competitive benchmarking mission, this is the clearest single data point: we are not in the decision set at all.

survey.text: Which ride-hailing brand in the UAE do you use most often?
survey.insight: 100% of respondents report Uber as their most frequently used brand. This aligns exactly with q5 and confirms the pattern is not a stated-preference artifact but reflects actual behavior. Careem's full consideration score (q4) but zero habitual-use score suggests it is a fallback app that respondents keep installed but rarely open first.

survey.text: On a scale of 0 to 10, how likely are you to recommend the brand to a friend or colleague? (0 = Not at all likely, 10 = Extremely likely)
survey.insight: The average score returned is 0 with a rating_n of 0, indicating no usable responses were captured for this question. Without a baseline NPS or likelihood-to-recommend score, we cannot track brand sentiment over time or compare it to industry benchmarks. This must be corrected in the next survey wave.

survey.text: Which of the following attributes apply to the brand? Select all that apply.
survey.insight: Only 2 respondents assigned any attribute to the brand: 1 selected "Reliable rides arrive on time" and 1 selected "Transparent fare pricing." No respondent attributed affordability, driver quality, app ease, safety, availability, promotions, or environmental responsibility to us. Given that the mission benchmarks on reliability, price, and driver quality specifically, scoring 1 of 5 on reliability and 0 of 5 on driver quality is a direct competitive deficit against the two attributes Uber is known to own.

survey.text: How likely are you to switch from your current ride-hailing brand in the UAE to a different one in the next 6 months? (1 = Not at all likely, 5 = Extremely likely)
survey.insight: Like q7, this question returned a 0 average with no valid ratings. We cannot determine how locked in respondents are to Uber or whether any switching window exists in the next 6 months. This is a critical gap for a competitor-benchmarking mission and must be recovered in follow-up fieldwork.

survey.text: If you were to switch your primary ride-hailing brand in the UAE, which brand would you most likely switch to?
survey.insight: 4 of 5 respondents said they would switch to Careem, and 1 said Bolt. the brand received zero switch-intent votes. This means that even if Uber experiences a service failure or price increase, we are not positioned to capture the resulting churn. Careem holds the default second-choice position that we should be competing for.

survey.text: In the past 2 weeks, have you talked about the brand with friends, family, or colleagues?
options: No, but I've thought about them
survey.insight: All 5 respondents selected "No, not at all" when asked whether they had discussed the brand recently. There was no negative buzz either, which rules out active reputation damage, but the complete absence of organic conversation means we have no earned media momentum in this segment. Word-of-mouth is the primary growth channel for ride-hailing adoption, so a zero score here is a structural growth barrier.

survey.text: Considering Guided Setup Wizard: a 3-step guided setup wizard that walks you through configuring your personal-finance app one step at a time. How appealing is this concept?
survey.insight: All rating fields for q2 returned zero values with null standard deviation and confidence intervals, indicating that numeric ratings were not captured for this question. The appeal score for Concept A cannot be reported. Do not draw conclusions from the average of 0.

survey.text: How relevant is the Guided Setup Wizard concept to your needs?
survey.insight: As with q2, all numeric values are zero and null, meaning no relevance signal was recorded for Concept A. This is a data-collection gap, not a finding.

survey.text: If the Guided Setup Wizard were available, how likely would you be to use it to set up a personal-finance app?
survey.insight: 100% landed on "Probably would buy", and no one chose the definitive positive or negative ends of the scale. This signals cautious, conditional interest rather than strong advocacy. The Wizard is a safe fallback, not a breakthrough product.

survey.insight: All numeric fields returned zero with null confidence intervals, matching the same data-collection failure seen in q2 through q4. Appeal scores for Concept B cannot be reported.

survey.insight: Same data gap as q7. No relevance signal can be reported for Concept B.

survey.text: How different is the AI Budget Builder from other onboarding concepts for personal-finance app options you have seen or used?
survey.insight: Same data gap as q7 and q8. No differentiation score can be stated for Concept B.

survey.text: If the AI Budget Builder were available, how likely would you be to use it to set up a personal-finance app?
survey.insight: Two respondents said "Probably would buy", two said "Definitely would NOT buy", and one was undecided. This is the most polarized result in the survey and a meaningful contrast to the Wizard's uniform moderate intent. The hard rejections are driven entirely by trust and data-security concerns, not by disinterest in automation.

survey.text: What's the best thing and the worst thing about the AI Budget Builder concept?
survey.insight: All five respondents named eliminating manual entry as the top benefit. All five also named distrust of AI categorization accuracy or anxiety about bank-data security as the primary concern. Two respondents used the word "trust" explicitly. One respondent referenced UAE bank security as partial reassurance, suggesting that local credibility signals could reduce friction.

survey.text: Which concept did you find most appealing overall?
survey.insight: Three respondents (60%) chose the AI Builder overall; two (40%) chose the Wizard. No respondent chose "None of these". The preference gap is small enough that trust improvements to the AI concept could shift the result, and trust failures could collapse it.

survey.text: Why?
survey.insight: The three AI Builder choosers each articulated the same core logic: manual entry is why they stopped using their last app, and the AI removes that friction at a recurring, not just onboarding, level. The two Wizard choosers both cited protecting dependents and needing to audit every step. This is a values split (efficiency vs. control) as much as a feature preference.
